answer:
**HYPOTHESIS (data-grounded answer to "What types of plant introductions were influenced by urban land use?")**

Two types of introductions were influenced by urban land use, through two complementary mechanisms:

(1) **Ornamental (Gardening) introductions were the type most favored by the historical urbanization era.** The pathway composition of new introductions shifted dramatically over time (χ² = 230.4, df = 6, p = 6.3×10⁻⁴⁷): Gardening rose from 16.8% of introductions before 1500 to 49.0% in 1901–1984 and 75.2% in 1985–2019 — the period coinciding with the region's strongest urban expansion — while Agriculture/Forestry introductions collapsed from 51.4% to 6.1% (Pearson residuals: +5.0 for Gardening and −5.5 for AgriForest in 1985–2019).

(2) **Among established alien flora on the ground, urban land use acts as a filter that favors Unintentionally introduced species and excludes AgriForest ones.** Across the 191 invaded plots in Barcelona province, pathway composition depends on surrounding urban cover (pooled counts × urban-cover bins, 2009 @ 500 m: χ² = 19.9, df = 6, p = 0.003): the Unintentional share of aliens rises from ~51% in plots with no urban cover to ~68% where urban cover exceeds 25–50%, and reaches 68.9% in Urban-habitat plots (n = 54; Croplands: 76.9% Unintentional). The probability of occurrence of Unintentional species increases with urban cover (logistic GLM, OR = 1.51 per SD of urban cover at 500 m, p = 0.076; OR = 1.89 per SD at 1000 m, p = 0.023), whereas AgriForest species drop out entirely in the most urbanized plots (0 of 120 aliens where urban cover > 50%; negative Spearman ρ = −0.16, p = 0.031 @ 1000 m) — their occurrence instead being driven by low elevation/warmer climate (elevation coef p = 0.027), i.e., lowland cropland contexts. Total alien richness also increases with urban cover over all 632 plots (Poisson IRR = 1.08 per +10% urban cover, p < 0.001). Gardening aliens, by contrast, do not concentrate in the most urbanized plots (presence OR = 0.83, p = 0.27) but are associated with **progressive landscape change** (share positively correlated with the 1956–2009 "progressive change" fraction, ρ = 0.15, p = 0.034) and persist in near-urban semi-natural habitats (highest shares in Coastal 53.5%, Wetlands 55.8%, Coniferous forests 87.5% of aliens) — consistent with ornamental species "spilling over" from gardens into recently transformed peri-urban landscapes.

Supporting trait pattern: Unintentional species are the most successful invaders (mean 9.6 invaded plots vs 3.9 Gardening, 2.3 AgriForest; invaded niche breadth 0.75 vs 0.45/0.62; Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.047), nearly all herbaceous (97%), whereas 48% of Gardening species are woody ornamentals (trees/shrubs) — the growth forms typically planted in urban and peri-urban greenery.

**Condensed hypothesis:** *Urban land use influenced plant introductions both historically and ecologically: the urbanization era (post-1900, especially post-1985) shifted the dominant introduction pathway toward ornamental/gardening introductions (~75% of recent introductions), while at the landscape scale increasing urban cover filters the established alien flora toward unintentionally introduced, ruderal, broad-niche herbs and excludes agriculture/forestry introductions, with gardening aliens persisting mainly in progressively changed, peri-urban coastal and wetland habitats.*

**Workflow executed** (all numbers reproducible from analysis/run_analysis.py → analysis/results.json):
1. Temporal trends: 4×3 contingency table; pathway shares per period; χ² test + Pearson residuals.
2. Plot-level: 191/632 invaded plots (481 alien records; n.gard+n.unint+n.agfo=n.total verified); Spearman correlations of pathway proportions and richness vs urban cover (3 years × 3 buffers); pooled composition × urban-bin χ²; binned pathway shares; logistic presence GLMs (z-scored urban, elevation, temperature); compact scale sensitivity (50/500/1000 m); landscape-change correlations; supplementary Poisson richness models (invaded and all plots); habitat summary table.
3. Species-level: 77 species (4 duplicates removed); pathway means + Kruskal-Wallis for invaded plots, niche breadth, habitat range, mrt; growth-form × pathway crosstab; family profile. Phylogenetic check kept secondary (per your instruction): 81 tips match species labels perfectly (incl. 4 duplicated-tip species); family-level note only (Asteraceae 14, Poaceae 10 species dominate), no formal PhylANOVA.

**Model choice & diagnostics:** count-based binomial GLMs (n_pw out of n_total) exhibited quasi-complete separation (|coef| > 10⁶, non-identifiable), so the main adjusted models are logistic presence/absence GLMs with z-scored covariates — all converged; Gardening model pseudo-R² = 0.012, accuracy 0.62. Elevation and temperature are collinear (VIF ≈ 10.6), so adjusted urban coefficients are corroborated by unadjusted rank correlations and binned shares, which agree in direction. Habitat effects are reported descriptively (binned table) rather than as dummies, because rare habitat levels (1–3 plots) drove the separation.

**Deviations from approved plan (disclosed):** (i) main adjusted model switched from count-binomial to presence-logistic GLMs due to quasi-separation; (ii) habitat dummies removed from GLMs (handled descriptively); (iii) formal phylogenetic test replaced by family-level note, as permitted.

**Limitations:** pathway proportions at plot level are small counts (median aliens/plot = 2), limiting power (some p-values marginal, 0.03–0.08); the species file has no plot-level urban cover, so Parts B and C are separate lines of evidence; proportion-based models with many zero plots are sensitive to model form (hence the multi-pronged corroboration).

payload.hypothesis: Urban land use influenced plant introductions both historically and ecologically: the urbanization era (post-1900, especially post-1985) shifted the dominant introduction pathway toward ornamental/gardening introductions (16.8% of introductions before 1500 vs 75.2% in 1985-2019; χ²=230.4, p=6e-47), while at the landscape scale increasing urban cover around plots shifts the composition of established aliens toward unintentionally introduced, ruderal, broad-niche herbs (Unintentional share 51%→68% across urban-cover bins, χ²=19.9, p=0.003; presence OR=1.5-1.9 per SD urban cover) and excludes agriculture/forestry introductions (0 aliens in the most urbanized plots), with gardening aliens persisting mainly in progressively changed peri-urban coastal and wetland habitats rather than dense urban cores.
payload.workflow: 1) Temporal: χ² and shares on the 4-period × 3-pathway contingency table. 2) Plot-level (191/632 invaded plots): Spearman correlations of pathway proportions/richness vs urban cover (3 years × 3 buffers), pooled pathway × urban-bin χ², binned pathway shares, logistic presence GLMs (z-scored urban, elevation, temperature) with scale sensitivity (50/500/1000 m), landscape-change correlations, supplementary Poisson richness models, habitat summary. 3) Species-level (77 species after dedup): pathway means and Kruskal-Wallis for invaded plots/niche breadth/habitat range/mrt, growth-form × pathway crosstab, family profile; phylogeny verified (81 tips = species labels) but kept as secondary family-level note. Diagnostics and the count-GLM quasi-separation deviation are documented in results.json and the handoff.
